subsystems.name: Slide scanning and image store
subsystems.role: turns glass slides into gigapixel digital images and serves them efficiently.
parts: whole-slide scanner (20× or 40×, roughly 0.5 or 0.25 µm per pixel)
pyramidal image format and DICOM pathology support

subsystems.name: Tissue detection and patching
subsystems.role: finds tissue, discards background and artefacts, and cuts the slide into model-sized tiles.

subsystems.name: Patch encoder
subsystems.role: the foundation model itself — maps each tile to a compact feature vector.

subsystems.name: Slide-level aggregator
subsystems.role: combines thousands of patch vectors into one slide representation, weighting the regions that matter.

subsystems.name: Task heads
subsystems.role: small classifiers trained on labelled cohorts for specific questions.

subsystems.name: Validation and monitoring layer
subsystems.role: proves the model works off the training site and keeps working.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the slide corpus
buildSteps.detail: Partner hospitals contribute consented diagnostic slides spanning organs, diseases, scanners and stain batches; diversity of sites matters more than raw volume for generalisation.

buildSteps.title: Scan and quality-control
buildSteps.detail: Slides are digitised, focussing is checked, and blurred, folded or pen-marked regions are flagged so they never enter training.

buildSteps.title: Tile the slides
buildSteps.detail: A tissue mask excludes blank glass; remaining tissue is cut into patches of roughly 256 pixels, about 128 µm across at 20×, with colour normalisation to reduce stain variation between labs.

buildSteps.title: Pretrain self-supervised
buildSteps.detail: A vision transformer is trained on hundreds of millions of patches using objectives such as masked-image modelling or self-distillation — no labels, just consistency between views of the same tissue. This runs for weeks on large GPU clusters.

buildSteps.title: Check the embeddings
buildSteps.detail: Frozen features are tested with simple linear probes on known tasks; if a linear classifier can already separate tumour grades, the representation is useful.

buildSteps.title: Train task heads
buildSteps.detail: Pathologist-labelled cohorts, often only hundreds to thousands of slides, are used to train the attention aggregator and a lightweight classifier on top of the frozen encoder.

buildSteps.title: Validate externally
buildSteps.detail: Performance is measured on held-out hospitals, different scanner models and different patient populations — the step where most research models fail.

buildSteps.title: Clear and deploy
buildSteps.detail: Regulatory review as a medical device, integration into the pathology viewer, and pathologist sign-off on every report; monitoring continues for scanner changes and population drift.

prerequisites.why: without digitised slides there is no training data at all; adoption is uneven, with many labs still partly glass-based.
self-supervised pretraining of a large vision transformer requires many accelerator-hours that only well-resourced groups command.
the methods that let models learn from unlabelled tiles are what make pathology foundation models possible, since labels are scarce.
data access, consent, and cross-institution governance are the real bottleneck, not algorithms.

prerequisites.tech: Paired molecular and genomic ground truth
prerequisites.why: predicting mutation status or gene expression from H&E requires cohorts where slides and sequencing exist for the same patients.
cleared tools exist for narrow tasks, but frameworks for continuously updated, multi-purpose models are still maturing.

pathway.milestone: general-purpose pathology encoders released and benchmarked across many tasks, plus a small number of narrowly cleared detection aids
pathway.unlocks: a shared starting point so hospitals need far fewer labelled slides per new task.

pathway.milestone: prospective multi-site trials showing the models hold up across scanners and populations
pathway.unlocks: clinical adoption beyond research and narrow niche tools.

pathway.milestone: slides combined with report text and genomics in one model; H&E-based prediction of molecular status offered as a triage aid
pathway.unlocks: genomic-grade information from a cheap routine stain, guiding which cases get sequencing.

pathway.milestone: hospital-wide deployment with continuous drift monitoring and clear liability rules for model-assisted diagnosis
pathway.unlocks: routine use in quality control, case triage and second-read, freeing pathologist time for difficult cases.
